definition: A Russia-attributed network of 100+ automated 'news' mirrors that republish pro-Kremlin Telegram channels and state media in dozens of languages. First exposed by France's VIGINUM (Feb 2024); tracked hourly by CheckFirst.

Flooding the open web with machine-scale propaganda aimed not at human readers but at contaminating the training and retrieval data of AI systems. Coined by the American Sunlight Project (Feb 2025). Audit evidence exists both for and against its effectiveness — see the measurement case file.

Russian operation running hundreds of LLM-rewritten fictional 'news' outlets and staged videos, laundered through fake journalist personas. Linked by VIGINUM to GRU Unit 29155. The most aggressive documented foreign actor in Hungary's 2026 campaign.

aliases: run by Social Design Agency & Structura
definition: The flagship Russian CIB operation since 2022: spoofed replicas of major Western news sites plus coordinated ad/comment amplification. EU- and US-sanctioned operators; 6,000+ public indicators via Meta. No documented Hungarian-language assets before the 2026 SDA plan.

Russia-aligned campaign that impersonates legitimate media brands (DW, Euronews, Le Monde) and floods fact-checkers with debunk-bait to inflate its perceived influence. Active in Hungary from March 2026, with little measured reach.

The PRC's highest-volume influence network — pioneer of AI news-anchor avatars and, per Microsoft, the first nation-state use of AI content against a foreign election (Taiwan 2024). Consistently negligible engagement; no documented Hungarian-language activity.

Sanctioned Moscow firms operating Doppelgänger under Kremlin direction (Sergei Kiriyenko's directorate, per the US DOJ affidavit). Reported by the FT to have drafted the covert pro-Fidesz social-media plan for Hungary's 2026 election.

Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference — the EU's institutional term for state-linked influence operations, used in the EEAS threat reports that provide the best cross-EU incident statistics (540 incidents in 2025; 27% involving AI).

Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior — Meta's enforcement category for networks of fake accounts working together to mislead. A CIB takedown is one of the strongest attribution signals available, because the platform sees the back-end evidence.

The open framework for describing influence-operation tactics and techniques — the ATT&CK equivalent for information operations, used by the EEAS to code FIMI incidents. This project's case files will carry DISARM technique tags in a coming phase.

Ben Nimmo's six-category scale for influence-operation impact, from confined to a single platform (1) to policy response or violence (6). Nearly every AI-assisted operation catalogued here was assessed at category 1–2: no breakout into authentic audiences.

The Fidesz-aligned Hungarian influencer network (€14.5m budget in 2024) that dominated domestic political advertising; researchers found it central to the ~90%-domestic share of 2026 election disinformation. Shut down after the election defeat.

Most election manipulation is cheap fakes — misleading edits, out-of-context clips — not AI. In the 2024 US cycle cheap fakes outnumbered AI content roughly seven to one (News Literacy Project, via the Knight Institute analysis); Hungary 2026 was notable precisely because generative AI took the lead role.

Whether Pravda-style mass publication is deliberate AI targeting ('grooming') or ordinary SEO spam with incidental AI contamination is genuinely contested. This site presents the audit numbers and the peer-reviewed counter-evidence side by side and does not claim more than the sources support.
